_doc: CANONICAL PARAMETER REGISTRY — one name, one unit, one meaning, for every semiconductor
quantity that reaches the loss engine, the requirement check, or the report.
This file is the SOURCE OF TRUTH for naming. Nothing downstream may invent a name: the
extractor writes canonical keys, the confirmation screen shows report_label, the engine
consumes engine_fields, and the report prints report_label. A quantity that appears under two
names in two layers is the defect class this registry exists to prevent (vg vs vg_drive, and
rdson vs rdson_25, are both live examples recorded below).
engine_fields is a LIST on purpose. More than one entry means the engine currently carries the
same physical quantity under several field names; every one of them must be written from the
same canonical value, and registry.audit_engine_block() checks exactly that.
plausible is a coarse order-of-magnitude sanity bound for the KEY. It is not the plausibility
gate: app/plausibility.py measures per-part bands from the vendor catalogues and checks
cross-field relations. This bound answers 'is this even the right kind of number', that one
answers 'is this consistent with 8948 real parts'.

si_mosfet.label: Silicon MOSFET
si_mosfet.note: Body-diode reverse recovery usually dominates turn-on.

sic_mosfet.label: SiC MOSFET
sic_mosfet.note: Strong positive R_DS(on) tempco; small Q_rr.

gan_hemt.label: GaN HEMT
gan_hemt.note: No body diode: Q_rr = 0 by construction. Reverse conduction has a gate-dependent offset voltage. Reject any profile asserting non-zero Q_rr.

igbt.label: IGBT
igbt.note: Conduction is V_ce0*I_avg + r_ce*I_rms^2, NOT I^2*R. Reject a profile carrying both V_CE_sat and R_DS_on.

sic_schottky.label: SiC Schottky diode
sic_schottky.note: Capacitive charge Q_c instead of reverse recovery.

bridge_rectifier.label: Bridge rectifier
bridge_rectifier.note: Line-frequency commutation; a totem-pole variant carries synchronous bottom FETs, which use the i2r form for those legs only.

measurement_basis_fields._doc: Mandatory on every energy and charge value. Not metadata - a correctness interlock. Convention B (see the plan) de-bundles E_oss and reverse-recovery charge out of a published E_on, which is only possible when these are known.

bundling._doc: How the value is used against a separate P_Eoss term. Extends the external spec's A7.1, which had no third state and would have blocked convention B.
bundling.raw: as published - REFUSE to run alongside a separate E_oss term
bundling.unknown: REFUSE to run alongside a separate E_oss term
bundling.de_bundled: E_oss and recovery charge subtracted from the anchor - ALLOWED alongside a separate E_oss term; the report must print the arithmetic

parameters.description: Total junction capacitance at a stated reverse voltage. Not consumed directly: vendors publish it at TWO voltages (typically 1 V and the rated V_R) and those two points fit C_j_grading, which sets both the Q_c voltage scaling and how much of the capacitive charge is dissipated rather than stored. The symbol CT used to be mapped onto C_iss, which is declared for the MOSFET classes only, so a rectifier's capacitance landed on a name its class does not carry and was dropped.

Grading coefficient m in C_j(v) = C0 * v^-m, fitted from two published capacitance points. It does two jobs: Q_c scales as V^(1-m) between the published reverse voltage and the bus, and the share of the capacitive charge DISSIPATED in the MOSFET rather than stored is 1/(2-m). m = 0 is a linear capacitor, for which that share is exactly the textbook 0.5 - which is why 0 is the default: an unknown m reproduces the previous result rather than silently changing it.

How many diode dies share one package, and therefore one case-to-sink interface. A dual common-cathode boost diode feeding both interleaved channels puts BOTH legs' loss through that interface while each junction sees only its own leg through R_th_jc. A design input, not a datasheet field: the designer knows which package is fitted and whether both legs are loaded.

Repetitive peak reverse voltage. The diode counterpart of V_DSS: the blocking requirement the GUI states before a datasheet is uploaded, not a loss parameter. The symbol VRRM used to be mapped onto V_DSS, which is a MOSFET-only key, so every diode's blocking rating landed on a name its class does not carry and was silently dropped.
Reverse-recovery time. Not consumed directly: it is one of the two published quantities from which Q_rr is reconstructed when Q_rr itself is not stated.
Peak reverse-recovery current. With t_rr it gives Q_rr = 0.5*t_rr*I_RRM for a triangular recovery, which is a stated approximation rather than a published charge.

si | sic | gan. Selects the MOSFET's default R_DS(on) temperature shape when no measured curve is supplied. The Diode carries is_sic instead and the Bridge has no equivalent, which is why this is declared for the MOSFET classes only.
Selects the conduction-loss form and the applicable physics interlocks. The engine field carries the coarse form ('si'/'sic'); the canonical key carries the full class.

Static on-resistance. MULTI-VALUED: the reference part publishes four entries (V_GS 15/18/20 V at 25 degC, plus 18 V at 175 degC). The engine field holds only the entry selected for the design's own V_GS at 25 degC; the rest live in the profile and are reached through select().

Normalised on-resistance versus junction temperature. Convex, so linear interpolation between two table endpoints overestimates in the middle - worth about 5.7 % on conduction loss, an order of magnitude less than the switching-energy error.
Normalised on-resistance versus drain current, evaluated at the local current at each line angle.
Input capacitance; sets the gate current-rise and fall times in the analytic switching model.
Reverse-transfer capacitance versus drain voltage. When present the Miller integral is computed from the curve instead of the Q_gd approximation.
Total gate charge. MUST carry the V_GS swing it was measured over - a Q_g quoted for 0 to 18 V is not the same part driven 0 to 15 V.
Gate-drain (Miller) charge. Estimated as 0.25*Q_g when absent, which was 37 % high on the reference part.
Gate threshold voltage.
Miller-plateau gate voltage. Derived as V_GS(th) + 2 V unless g_fs is known, in which case it is computed per-current and the switching energy becomes correctly superlinear.

Transconductance. Usually a table value. Without it the plateau voltage is constant and switching energy comes out strictly proportional to current; with it the plateau rises with current and the energy becomes superlinear.

Gate-drive voltage swing. A DESIGN choice, not a datasheet value - no upload can supply it. TWO ENGINE FIELDS carry it: 'vg' in the switching model and 'vg_drive' in the gate-loss term. They are the same physical quantity and must always be written together; writing only one is the defect that put a 12 V gate loss into the report while switching used 15 V.
Turn-ON gate resistance, external plus driver source. A DESIGN choice. Couples only to E_on. Falls back to R_g_common when unset.
Turn-OFF gate resistance, external plus driver sink. A DESIGN choice. Couples only to E_off.
Gate resistance used when the on and off paths are not stated separately. Switching energy scales roughly linearly with it, so a placeholder here is a ~2x lever.
Internal gate resistance from the datasheet. Adds to the external path; reported so the designer can include it in R_g_on / R_g_off.

Published turn-on energy at a stated test point. NOT consumed as a fixed per-cycle energy: it anchors the switching model. A published E_on bundles the device's own C_oss and the freewheeling device's charge, both of which this engine counts separately - so convention B de-bundles it before anchoring. The measurement basis is what makes that possible.

Published turn-off energy at a stated test point. Anchors E_off independently of E_on; the two anchor factors differing widely is a signal that the model shape is wrong, not that the magnitude needs scaling.

Turn-on energy versus drain current. Has a large non-zero intercept - measured at 69 % of the full-current value at 2 A on the reference part - so linear-through-origin scaling understates badly at low current, which is where a sinusoidal converter spends most of the line cycle.
Turn-off energy versus drain current.
Turn-on energy at the elevated junction temperature. When present the engine interpolates linearly in T_j between the two curves instead of applying a scalar tempco.
Turn-off energy at the elevated junction temperature.
Bus voltage the switching-energy curves were measured at. Switching energy is scaled by V_bus / V_test.
Junction temperature of the reference switching-energy curve.
Junction temperature of the hot switching-energy curve.
Fractional temperature coefficient of switching energy, used only when no hot curve is available.

Output-capacitance stored energy versus drain voltage, evaluated at the ACTUAL bus voltage. Estimating it from die area (0.9e-6 / R_DS(on)) was 3.4x high on the reference SiC part, because that scaling is calibrated on silicon superjunction.
Drain leakage versus junction temperature. Absent means the blocking-loss term is zero, which is a placeholder rather than a measurement.
Body-diode forward voltage.
Body-diode reverse-recovery charge. Must be zero for gan_hemt.
Drain-source breakdown rating. Not a loss parameter: it is the requirement the GUI states before a datasheet is uploaded.
Continuous drain current, usually published at two case temperatures.
Maximum junction temperature. Consumed by the thermal check, not the loss engine.

Junction-to-case thermal resistance. A multi-die package publishes it TWICE - per leg and per device - and the junction sees the per-leg (larger) figure; the per-device number describes the whole package. Not flagged multi_valued because the two are distinguished by scope rather than by any measurement condition, and see dies_per_package for how the shared case is handled.
Case-to-sink thermal resistance - the mounting interface. A DESIGN choice: no datasheet can supply it.
Transient thermal impedance as an R-tau Foster ladder, for cycle-by-cycle junction excursion.
Commutation-loop stray inductance; adds 0.5*L*I_off^2 to turn-off energy. A LAYOUT choice.
Which switching-energy model is active. A MODEL OPTION, not a measurement - the report must state which one produced the number.
Turn-off energy anchor factor. Under convention B this carries E_off,datasheet / E_off,analytic at the test point.
Tolerance multiplier: 1.0 for typical, above 1 for a worst-case sign-off run.
Switching-energy tolerance multiplier.
Output-capacitance energy tolerance multiplier.
Gate-charge tolerance multiplier.
Forward voltage versus forward current at the reference temperature.
Forward voltage curve at the elevated junction temperature; enables per-point T_j interpolation instead of a scalar tempco.
Forward-voltage temperature coefficient, used only when no hot curve exists. Negative for silicon, positive for SiC.
Temperature of the reference forward-voltage curve.
Temperature of the hot forward-voltage curve.
Dynamic series resistance of the forward characteristic. Zero understates the benefit of paralleling devices.
Selects capacitive charge Q_c over reverse recovery Q_rr. Derived from device_class; kept because the engine dataclass still carries the boolean.

Capacitive (junction) charge of a Schottky diode, published at a stated V_R. The loss engine consumes it AT THE BUS VOLTAGE, so a value stated at a different V_R is scaled there rather than used as published. Also the term convention B subtracts out of a published E_on when this device is the fixture's freewheeling element.
Reverse-recovery charge. Estimated as 0.5*t_rr*I_o when only t_rr is published.
Reverse-recovery charge versus commutation di/dt.
Reverse-recovery charge versus forward current.
Reverse-recovery charge temperature coefficient.

Fraction of the silicon diode's reverse-recovery energy dissipated in the MOSFET rather than in the diode. An ASSUMED partition, not a datasheet quantity: it scales the largest single MOSFET loss term, so it is stamped and reported, never silent.
Forward-recovery energy.

Reverse leakage versus junction temperature, quoted AT A STATED REVERSE VOLTAGE which is normally the part's rated V_R, not the bus. Schottky leakage rises steeply with reverse voltage, so a rated-V_R figure used at a lower bus is a conservative upper bound - reported as one rather than scaled by a law nobody measured.
Forward-voltage tolerance multiplier.
Reverse-recovery-charge tolerance multiplier.
Capacitive-charge tolerance multiplier.
Output capacitance. The engine uses the stored-energy curve E_oss(V_DS) rather than C_oss directly, because energy is what is dissipated; C_oss is carried for the record.
Output charge. Reported; the loss model works from E_oss.
Maximum power dissipation at a stated case temperature. Used today only to ESTIMATE R_th(j-c) when the datasheet does not state it; with a real R_th(j-c) extracted, that estimate is no longer needed.
Storage temperature range. Not consumed by any calculation; carried so the extracted profile is a faithful record of the datasheet rather than only the parts we happen to use.
Gate leakage current. Reported, not used in the loss model.

Published total switching energy, E_on + E_off at the test point. Reference only: the engine anchors E_on and E_off SEPARATELY, because their anchor factors differing is diagnostic of the model shape rather than of its magnitude.

Average rectified forward current. The diode/bridge counterpart of I_D: it is the requirement the GUI states before a datasheet is uploaded, not a loss parameter. MULTI-VALUED - vendors publish it with and without a heatsink, and taking the first number silently discards an operating point.

Single half-sine surge current rating. Not a loss parameter: the Chapter 8 bridge-surge gate checks the cold-start inrush against it. Absent from the parametric catalogue on every part, which is why that gate reports OPEN - and present in the datasheet TABLE, which is why extraction closes it.
Fusing I2t rating, in A^2s. Paired with I_FSM in the Chapter 8 startup-path stress check. The unit has no SI entry of its own; stored as a bare number.
Full-diode bridge, or a synchronous variant whose bottom legs are MOSFETs using the i2r conduction form.
Devices in parallel. A DESIGN choice.
Devices in parallel on the bridge's top legs.
Devices in parallel on the bridge's bottom legs.
Worst-case current-sharing fraction between paralleled devices.
On-resistance of the synchronous bottom-leg FETs in a totem-pole bridge.
Normalised on-resistance versus temperature for the bottom-leg FETs.
Gate charge of the bottom-leg FETs; they commutate at line frequency, not switching frequency.
Gate-drive voltage for the bottom-leg FETs. A DESIGN choice.
Junction-to-case thermal resistance of the bottom-leg devices.
Case-to-sink thermal resistance of the bottom-leg devices. A DESIGN choice.
